---
title: "Confidence Interval for Difference of Population Means"
format: html
editor: visual
self-contained: true

## Question 1 (4 points)

A woodworking instructor wants to compare the average time it takes to complete a particular type of dovetail joint using two different saws: a traditional hand saw and a Japanese pull saw. The instructor randomly assigns 30 students to each saw type and records their completion times (in minutes). They find the following: $n_{\text{Hand}} = n_{\text{Pull}} = 30$, $s_{\text{Hand}}^2 = 11.5, s_{\text{Pull}}^2 = 13$, and $\bar{x}_{\text{Hand}} = 22.8, \bar{x}_{\text{Pull}} = 20.1$.

In the code block below, construct a 90% confidence interval for the difference in population mean times to complete the dovetail joint (traditional hand saw minus Japanese pull saw). THEN INTERPRET THE INTERVAL IN CONTEXT.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
n1 <- 30
n2 <- 30
xbar1 <- 22.8
xbar2 <- 20.1
s21 <- 11.5
s22 <- 13
max(s21, s22) <= 4*min(s21, s22)

sp <- sqrt(((n1-1)*s21 + (n2-1)*s22)/(n1+n2-2))
alpha <- 0.1
t_quant <- qt(1-alpha/2, n1+n2-2)

xbar1 - xbar2 + c(-1, 1)*t_quant*sp*sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2)
```

[We are 90% confident that the true difference in average completion times between the Traditional Hand Saw and Japanese Pull Saw is between 1.1894 and 4.2106 minutes.]{style="color: red;"}

## Question 2 (4 points)

A sports scientist wants to compare the average 5K race times (in minutes) for two groups of recreational runners: those who follow a low-carb diet and those who follow a high-carb diet. The scientist collects the following race times from two random samples of runners.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
low_carb <- c(27.3, 28.7, 26.5, 30.2, 29.5, 30.8, 31.2, 28.0, 27.9, 29.0,
              30.5, 31.1, 29.7, 28.3, 27.5, 29.8, 30.2, 31.5, 30.0, 29.2,
              28.9, 29.4, 28.7, 27.8, 29.9, 30.1, 28.5, 28.6, 30.0, 29.1)

high_carb <- c(26.2, 25.8, 24.5, 27.9, 26.1, 27.2, 25.6, 26.7, 27.5, 26.0,
               24.9, 26.3, 26.1, 25.7, 26.5, 27.1, 27.3, 26.8, 25.4, 27.6,
               26.2, 25.9, 26.0, 26.7, 27.4, 25.6, 25.8, 27.3, 26.5, 26.9)
```

In the code block below, use these data to construct a 99% confidence interval for the difference in mean running times (low-carb minus high carb). THEN INTERPRET THE INTERVAL IN CONTEXT.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
max(var(low_carb), var(high_carb)) <= 4*min(var(low_carb), var(high_carb))

t.test(low_carb, high_carb, var.equal = TRUE, conf.level = 0.99)$conf.int
```

[We are 99% confident that the true difference between mean race times for the low- and high-carb groups is between 2.1634 and 3.5965 minutes.]{style="color: red;"}

## Question 3 (4 points)

A researcher is studying two different teaching methods for high school algebra. One method is inquiry-based learning, and the other is a traditional lecture approach. Students’ final exam scores (out of 100 points) were recorded from two separate random samples of students, one for each teaching method. They find the following: $n_{\text{Inq}} = 35, n_{\text{Trad}} = 40$, $s_{\text{Inq}}^2 = 25, s_{\text{Trad}}^2 = 144$, and $\bar{x}_{\text{Inq}} = 83, \bar{x}_{\text{Trad}} = 81$.

In the code block below, construct a 95% confidence interval for the difference in population mean exam scores (traditional minus inquiry-based). THEN INTERPRET THE INTERVAL IN CONTEXT.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
n1 <- 35
n2 <- 40
xbar1 <- 83
xbar2 <- 81
s21 <- 25
s22 <- 144
max(s21, s22) <= 4*min(s21, s22)

df <- (s21/n1 + s22/n2)^2/(s21^2/(n1^2*(n1-1)) + s22^2/(n2^2*(n2-1)))
alpha <- 0.05
t_quant <- qt(1-alpha/2, df)

xbar2 - xbar1 + c(-1, 1)*t_quant*sqrt(s21/n1 + s22/n2)
```

[We are 95% confident that the true difference in mean final exam scores for the traditional and inquiry-based learning methods is between -6.1650 and 2.1650 points.]{style="color: red;"}

## Question 4 (4 points)

A cognitive psychologist wants to compare the time spent analyzing each move (in seconds) between expert and novice chess players. Two random samples were taken: one of expert players and one of novice players. The times (in seconds) taken to analyze a particular middle-game position are shown below.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
expert <- c(45, 42, 48, 50, 43, 47, 49, 46, 50, 41,
            44, 46, 47, 48, 45, 46, 44, 45, 43, 46,
            42, 44, 45, 47, 49, 45, 46, 47, 45, 44)

novice <- c(61, 58, 64, 63, 67, 70, 62, 65, 69, 68,
            66, 63, 67, 65, 64, 66, 68, 69, 70, 64,
            67, 65, 68, 69, 63, 62, 64, 65, 68, 70)
```

In the code block below, construct a 99% confidence interval for the difference in population mean time spent (expert minus novice). THEN INTERPRET THE INTERVAL IN CONTEXT.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
max(var(expert), var(novice)) <= 4*min(var(expert), var(novice))

t.test(expert, novice, var.equal = TRUE, conf.level = 0.99)$conf.int
```

[We are 99% confident that the true difference in mean time spent between experts and novices is between -21.8697 and -18.1969 seconds.]{style="color: red;"}
